source.statement: At h=1/beta and kappa=beta/alpha, distance_N<=exp(-N/(2*kappa))*R; N>=2*kappa*log(R/epsilon) suffices for distance_N<=epsilon.
source.assumptions: Standing C2 Euclidean objective, alpha-convex/beta-smooth, supplied minimizer; positive alpha,beta for condition number and prescribed step, positive epsilon for target accuracy. Ordinary log ratio requires R>0. No positive lower bound on N is needed: N0 is valid when epsilon>=R.
source.scope: Sufficient iteration threshold, not an optimal/necessary stopping time, runtime count, floating-point computation guarantee or improved Exercise3.2 rate.

exact_apis.name: Nat.le_ceil

recommended_interface.alternative: An unconditional Lean threshold with totalized log is mathematically valid if R0 separately proved; reader must still distinguish source positive-log domain from this totalized extension. Conditional R>0 interface is cleaner.

proof_route: Invoke existing actual-iterate distance parent at h=beta inverse and combine its conjuncts to obtain exp(-(alpha/beta*N)/2)*R control.
Split R=0 versusR>0 using norm nonnegativity. Zero case gives distance<=0 directly from bound and epsilon>0, all naturalN, no log evaluation.

For positiveR, multiply threshold by alpha/(2beta)>0 or divide by2(beta/alpha)>0 to obtain log(R/epsilon)<=(alpha/beta*N)/2. Positivity of alpha,beta is load-bearing; log may be negative and must not be assumed nonnegative.
Apply Mathlib exponential/logarithm comparison to show exp(-(alpha/beta*N)/2)*R<=epsilon; combine with actual distance bound.
Optionally instantiate natural ceiling via Nat.le_ceil. No requirementepsilon<R orN>0: ifepsilon>=R, threshold<=0 soN0 legitimately suffices.
